addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- harness-architect: Arquiteto do MommaERP. Emite ADRs para decisões com reversibilidade difícil, revisa migrações SQL críticas, e resolve impasses técnicos do loop Builder-Evaluator. Invocado quando há migration nova, mudança de contrato/API, ou falha após 2 iterações de builder. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- harness-builder: Implementa features, fixes e refactors no MommaERP (Gidape). Usa TDD-first, escrevendo testes que falham antes de implementar. Invocado pelo orchestrator após aprovação do plan. Use para código não-UI: hooks, services, migrations, utilities. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Bash, Glob, Grep)

- harness-clarifier: Transforma pedidos ambíguos em specs estruturadas para o MommaERP. Conduz Q&A com o humano (até 10 perguntas, rodadas de 4) e produz spec.md com Context/Requirements/Acceptance. Para features e fixes. (Tools: Read, Write, Glob)

- harness-debugger: Root-cause analysis de bugs no MommaERP. Invocado quando root-cause não é óbvio no pedido de fix. Conhece os landmines históricos do projeto. Entrega RCA estruturado com evidências antes de propor fix. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep)

- harness-doc-writer: Escritor de documentação do MommaERP. Lê o diff do que foi implementado e atualiza diretamente as docs de usuário (MkDocs) e o CHANGELOG.md. Invocado na Phase 4 antes do push. Escreve exclusivamente em pt-BR. Use para sincronizar docs de usuário após uma feature implementada e atualizar o CHANGELOG. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- harness-evaluator: QA cético e independente do MommaERP. Avalia código implementado com rubrica por tipo de artifact. Nunca avalia o próprio trabalho — é sempre chamado após o builder. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep)

- harness-frontend-builder: Especialista em frontend React do MommaERP. Gemini 3 (gemini-3.1-pro-preview) escreve o código React/TypeScript completo. Invocado para qualquer trabalho de UI — nova página, redesign, componente novo, layout. Gemini implementa o frontend; Claude não toca UI depois. (Tools: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep)

- harness-frontend-reviewer: Revisor SOTA de frontend do MommaERP. RODA verificações determinísticas (lint/tsc/build/grep validators), compara contra a página canônica de referência, e faz revisão adversarial por lentes (design system, responsivo, dark mode, React, a11y). Roda em paralelo com harness-security-reviewer antes do evaluator. Emite smoke checklist cirúrgico para o que não dá pra verificar sem render. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- harness-git-miner: Minerador de retrabalho do MommaERP. Varre o histórico git em busca de defeitos que escaparam dos gates (commit feat/refactor seguido de fix nos mesmos arquivos) e propõe entradas de learning. Use sob demanda para auto-melhorar o harness com base no uso real, ou quando o usuário pedir uma varredura de padrões de erro. (Tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob)

- harness-memory-updater: Curator do playbook de learnings do MommaERP (modo ACE). Recebe um defeito (de RCA do debugger, de proposta do git-miner, ou sinalizado pelo usuário) e o destila em 1 delta append-only no arquivo de learning do domínio certo, com dedup e contadores. Também consolida patterns positivos no memory-bank. Nunca reescreve — só adiciona ou incrementa. Use após o evaluator aprovar uma feature, após um RCA, ou quando um defeito for sinalizado. (Tools: Read, Edit, Glob, Grep)

- harness-planner: Expande spec.md em PRD detalhado para features L/XL do MommaERP. Invocado pelo orchestrator apenas para features de alta complexidade (múltiplos módulos, nova tabela principal, novo workflow de negócio). Produz breakdown de steps, estimativa e risk matrix. (Tools: Read, Write, Glob, Grep)

- harness-security-reviewer: Revisor de segurança especializado em Supabase/RLS do MommaERP. Verifica RLS, autenticação, isolamento multi-loja e proteção de dados sensíveis. Invocado condicionalmente quando o diff toca áreas de segurança. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## supabase-mcp-server
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, use `list_tables` to understand the existing structure
- When debugging issues, start with `get_logs` and `get_advisors` before making changes
- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Use `apply_migration` carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

- prd: Generate a Product Requirements Document (PRD) for a new feature. Use when planning a feature, starting a new project, or when asked to create a PRD. Triggers on: create a prd, write prd for, plan this feature, requirements for, spec out.
- ralph: Convert PRDs to prd.json format for the Ralph autonomous agent system. Use when you have an existing PRD and need to convert it to Ralph's JSON format. Triggers on: convert this prd, turn this into ralph format, create prd.json from this, ralph json.
- recap-do-dia: Lê tudo que foi feito hoje (sessões Claude Code, commits git, tasks Todoist) e gera o mix certo de conteúdo pra X — short posts diários + thread candidata pro banco semanal — escrevendo no Notion para copy-paste manual.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

-- distribuição de visibilidade: quantos produtos têm linhas de visibility e quantas
SELECT
  (SELECT count(*) FROM produtos_master WHERE ativo) AS produtos_ativos,
  (SELECT count(DISTINCT produto_master_id) FROM produto_loja_visibility) AS produtos_com_visibility,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM produto_loja_visibility WHERE loja_id=4) AS rows_lago_sul;

-- já existe peito de frango? evitar duplicata
SELECT id, nome, nome_normalizado, setor, unidade_medida, ativo
FROM produtos_master
WHERE nome ILIKE '%frango%' OR nome ILIKE '%peito%'
ORDER BY nome;

content.text: Setor **COMIDAS**, unidade **kg**. Os produtos ativos em COMIDAS seguem nome em CAIXA ALTA (FRANGO GRELHADO, CALDO DE FRANGO...), então vou cadastrar como `PEITO DE FRANGO IN NATURA`. Insiro o produto + a linha de visibilidade só para Lago Sul numa transação única:

input.query:
WITH novo AS (
  INSERT INTO produtos_master (nome, nome_normalizado, setor, unidade_medida, ativo)
  VALUES ('PEITO DE FRANGO IN NATURA', 'peito de frango in natura', 'COMIDAS', 'kg', true)
  RETURNING id, nome, setor, unidade_medida, ativo, codigo_interno
),
vis AS (
  INSERT INTO produto_loja_visibility (produto_master_id, loja_id, ativo)
  SELECT id, 4, true FROM novo
  ON CONFLICT (produto_master_id, loja_id) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING produto_master_id, loja_id
)
SELECT n.id, n.nome, n.setor, n.unidade_medida, n.ativo, n.codigo_interno,
       v.loja_id AS visivel_para_loja
FROM novo n LEFT JOIN vis v ON v.produto_master_id = n.id;
